ait: aiō, ais, ait — to say (defective verb) (3rd sg. pres.)
alios: alius, alia, aliud — other, another (m. acc. pl.)

animum: animus, -ī (m.) — mind, spirit, feelings, heart (acc. sg.)
ardebant: ardeō, -ēre, arsī — to burn, blaze; be eager, be on fire (3rd pl. impf.)
aut: aut (conj.) — or; aut… aut, either… or
casus: cāsus, -ūs (m.) — fall; chance, misfortune, disaster (acc./nom. pl.; nom. sg.)

dido: Dīdō, Dīdōnis (f.) — Dido, queen of Carthage (nom. sg.)
divom: dīvus, -ī (m.) — god (gen. pl., old form = dīvōrum)
domus: domus, -ūs (f.) — house, home, dwelling (nom. sg.) · gen. sg. (of the house; domus scelus)
ducit: dūcō, -ere, duxī, ductum — to lead, guide (3rd sg. pres.)
dum: dum (conj.) — while; until (+ subj., of a goal looked forward to)

enim: enim (conj., postpositive) — for, indeed, in fact
erat: sum, esse, fuī — to be (3rd sg. impf.)

et: et — and; also, even; et… et: both… and
ex: ex, ē (prep. + abl.) — out of, from

ferant: ferō, ferre, tulī, lātum — to carry, bear, carry off (3rd pl. pres. subj.)

finibus: fīnis, -is (m./f.) — boundary, border; pl. territory (abl./dat. pl.)
finis: fīnis, fīnis (m./f.) — end, limit, boundary (nom. sg.)
fortis: fortis, -e — brave, strong (m./f. gen. sg.; also nom. sg.; acc. pl. = fortēs)

gentis: gēns, gentis (f.) — race, people, nation (gen. sg.) · also acc. pl., -is for -ēs (gentīs superbās)
genus: genus, generis (n.) — race, family, birth, kind (nom./acc. sg.)
gesserat: gerō, gerere, gessī, gestum — to carry; to wage (war), conduct (3rd sg. pluperf.)
gyan: Gyās, Gyae (m.) — Gyas, Trojan captain (acc. sg., Greek form Gyān)
hac: hāc (adv.) — on this side, this way; hāc… hāc, on this side… on that (orig. f. abl. sg. of hic)
haec: hic, haec, hoc — this; haec (n. pl.), these things, these words (n. nom./acc. pl.; f. nom. sg.)
his: hic, haec, hoc — this; pl. these (dat./abl. pl.)
honorem: honor (honōs), honōris (m.) — honour; offering, sacrifice (acc. sg.)
honores: honor (honōs), honōris (m.) — honour, esteem; offering, sacrifice (nom./acc. pl.)
honos: honor (honōs), honōris (m.) — honour, esteem, reward (nom. sg., older form honos)
iam: iam (adv.) — now, already; iam… iam, now… now
illa: ille, illa, illud — that; she, that woman (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
ille: ille, illa, illud — that; he, that man (m. nom. sg.)
in: in (prep.) — + acc. into, onto, against; + abl. in, on
infandos: infandus, -a, -um — unspeakable, dreadful, abominable (m. acc. pl.)
ingens: ingēns, ingentis — huge, enormous, mighty (nom. sg.) · (n. acc. sg.: bellum ingens) · also n. acc. sg. (templum ingens)
insequitur: īnsequor, īnsequī, īnsecūtus sum — to follow, follow on, come next (3rd sg. pres.) · to pursue, hound (of fortune)
ipsa: ipse, ipsa, ipsum — herself, she herself; the very (f. nom. sg.)
ipse: ipse, ipsa, ipsum — himself, herself, itself; the very (m. nom. sg.)
labores: labor, labōris (m.) — toil, labour, hardship (acc./nom. pl.)
magnum: magnus, -a, -um — great, large, vast (m. acc. sg.; n. nom./acc. sg.)
manus: manus, -ūs (f.) — hand; handiwork (acc. pl.; also nom./gen. sg., nom./voc. pl.)
mecum: mē + cum — with me (cum enclitic after the pronoun)
mediisque: medius, -a, -um — middle, in the middle of (m./n. abl./dat. pl.) + -que 'and'
medio: medius, -a, -um — middle, in the middle of (m./n. abl./dat. sg.)
mentem: mēns, mentis (f.) — mind, heart, feelings (acc. sg.)
mihi: ego, meī — I; mihi, to/for me (dat.)
moenia: moenia, -ium (n. pl.) — walls, city walls (nom./acc. pl.)
navis: nāvis, -is (f.) — ship (acc. pl., = nāvēs; also nom./gen. sg.)
nec: nec, neque — and not, nor; nec… nec, neither… nor
neque: neque (nec) — and not, nor; neque enim, for indeed… not
nos: ego, meī — I; nōs, we, us (nom./acc. pl.)
nova: novus, -a, -um — new, fresh, strange (f. nom./abl. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
nubes: nūbēs, nūbis (f.) — cloud (nom./acc. pl.; nom. sg.)
nunc: nunc (adv.) — now, at present; nunc… nunc, now… now
obstipuit: obstipescō (obstupescō), -ere, -stipuī — to be stunned, struck dumb (3rd sg. perf.)
olim: ōlim (adv.) — once, formerly; one day, in time to come
omnia: omnis, -e — all, every; omnia, all things, everything (n. nom./acc. pl.)
omnis: omnis, -e — all, every (acc. pl., = omnēs; also nom./gen. sg.)
orbem: orbis, orbis (m.) — circle; orbis terrārum, the world (acc. sg.)
origine: orīgō, orīginis (f.) — origin, source, lineage (abl. sg.)
os: ōs, ōris (n.) — mouth, face, look (acc./nom. sg.)
parant: parō, -āre — to prepare, make ready; + inf. to set about (3rd pl. pres.)
parentes: parēns, parentis (m./f.) — parent; pl. forefathers (nom./acc. pl.)
passus: patior, patī, passus sum — to suffer, endure, allow (perf. part., m. nom. sg.)
pater: pater, patris (m.) — father (nom. sg.) · also voc. sg. (pater optume)
per: per (prep. + acc.) — through, across, throughout; by
pergama: Pergama, -ōrum (n. pl.) — citadel of Troy; Troy (acc./nom. pl.)
petit: petō, petere, petīvī, petītum — to seek, make for, aim at (3rd sg. pres.)
post: post (adv.; prep. + acc.) — afterwards, hereafter; after, behind
primo: prīmus, -a, -um — first, earliest, outermost (m./n. abl./dat. sg.)
prior: prior, prius — former, earlier, first (of two) (m./f. nom. sg.)
qua: quā (adv.) — where, by which way; in any way (after sī); also quī/quis, f. abl. sg.
quae: quī, quae, quod — who, which (rel., f. nom. sg.; f./n. nom./acc. pl.) · interrog. adj., what? which? (f. nom. sg.: quae sententia)
quam: quī, quae, quod — who, which (rel., f. acc. sg.); quam (adv.), how; than · prius… quam (conj.), before, until · indef. after sī/nē, any, some (f. acc. sg.: si quam)
quem: quī, quae, quod — who, whom (rel. or interrog., m. acc. sg.) · quis, quid after sī, nē — any(one), some(one) (indef., m. acc. sg.: sī quem)
qui: quī, quae, quod — who, which (rel. pron., m. nom. sg./pl.) · interrog. adj./pron., who? which? (m. nom. sg./pl.: Sed vos qui tandem)
quibus: quī, quae, quod — who, which (rel., abl./dat. pl.) · interrog. adj., what? which? (abl./dat. pl.)
quid: quis, quid — who, what (interrog., n. nom./acc. sg.) · also adverbially, why? (n. acc. sg.)
quis: quī, quae, quod — who (rel., dat./abl. pl., old form = quibus); also quis, who? (interrog.) · also indefinite quis, anyone (after nē/neu, m. nom. sg.); quis locus, which place? (interrog. adj.)
quod: quī, quae, quod — which (rel., n. nom./acc. sg.); quod (conj.), because, that · also interrog. adj., what? (n. nom./acc. sg.: quod genus)
quoque: quoque (adv.) — also, too (follows the word it stresses)
quos: quī, quae, quod — who, which (rel. or interrog., m. acc. pl.)
rapidum: rapidus, -a, -um — snatching, consuming, devouring; swift (m./n. acc. sg.)
refulsit: refulgeō, -ēre, refulsī — to flash back, shine out, gleam (3rd sg. perf.)
regia: rēgius, -a, -um — royal, queenly (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
reliquias: reliquiae, -ārum (f. pl.) — remains, remnants, survivors (acc. pl.)
rerum: rēs, reī (f.) — thing, matter; pl. circumstances, fortunes (gen. pl.)
res: rēs, reī (f.) — thing, matter, affair; state (nom. sg.; nom./acc. pl.)
scindit: scindō, scindere, scidī, scissum — to split, cleave, divide (3rd sg. pres.)
se: suī (reflexive pron.) — himself, herself, itself, themselves (acc.; also abl. sē)
seu: seu (sīve) — or if; seu… seu, whether… or
sic: sīc (adv.) — so, thus, in this way
sidera: sīdus, sīderis (n.) — star, constellation; pl. the sky (acc./nom. pl.)
sidonia: Sīdōnius, -a, -um — of Sidon, Phoenician, Carthaginian (f. nom. sg.)
simul: simul (adv.) — at the same time, together
sive: sīve (seu) — or if; sīve… sīve, whether… or
talem: tālis, -e — such, of such a kind (m./f. acc. sg.)
talia: tālis, -e — such, of such a kind; tālia, such things, such words (n. acc./nom. pl.)
tam: tam (adv.) — so, so much, to such a degree
tanta: tantus, -a, -um — so great, such (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
tenebat: teneō, -ēre, tenuī, tentum — to hold, keep, grasp (3rd sg. impf.)
terrae: terra, -ae (f.) — earth, land, country (gen./dat. sg.; nom. pl.)
teucri: Teucer, Teucrī (m.) — Teucer, early king of Troy (gen. sg.)
teucrorum: Teucrī, -ōrum (m. pl.) — the Teucrians, Trojans (from Teucer, an early king of Troy) (gen. pl.)
teucrum: Teucrī, -ōrum (m. pl.) — Teucrians, Trojans (gen. pl., archaic -um for -ōrum)
tibi: tū, tuī — you (sg.); tibi, to/for you (dat.)
tum: tum (adv.) — then, at that time; next
tuta: tūtus, -a, -um — safe, sheltered (n. nom./acc. pl.; f. nom./abl. sg.)
tyria: Tyrius, -a, -um — Tyrian, of Tyre (f. nom./abl. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
vastabat: vastō, -āre — to lay waste, ravage, devastate (3rd sg. impf.)
venus: Venus, Veneris (f.) — Venus, goddess of love, mother of Aeneas (nom. sg.)
vides: videō, vidēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see, behold (2nd sg. pres.)
viri: vir, virī (m.) — man, hero, husband (nom. pl.; gen. sg.)
vis: vīs, vīs (f.) — force, power, violence; pl. vīrēs, strength (nom. sg.)
vocant: vocō, -āre — to call, name, summon (3rd pl. pres.)
vos: tū, vōs — you (2nd pers. pl. pron.) (nom./acc. pl.)
